title: Derived constant/limit adjunction with its actual projection counit
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] admitting inverse limits of countable towers. Put $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system], with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Assume the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal T)$ exist [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and every complex in $\mathcal T$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal T)}(Z,I)=0$ for every acyclic $Z$. Let $L=\lim:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ and let $RL$ be its total right derived functor computed by $RL(QI)=Q(LI)$ on such resolutions. Let $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$ be the constant tower, also denoting its termwise exact derived functor by $\Delta$, and let $e_n:D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be evaluation. Define $\pi_{n,B}:RL(B)\to e_nB$ on a tower resolution $q:M\to I$ by the inverse-limit projection $LI\to I_n$ followed by $(Qq_n)^{-1}$, with the canonical resolution identifications. The ordinary adjunction $\Delta\dashv L$ induces a canonical adjunction $\Delta:D(\mathcal A)\rightleftarrows D(\mathcal T):RL$ whose counit $\epsilon_B:\Delta RL(B)\to B$ satisfies $e_n(\epsilon_B)=\pi_{n,B}$ under $e_n\Delta=\mathrm{id}$, naturally in $B$ and independently of its resolution. For any category $\mathcal J$, functors $C:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal A)$, $B:\mathcal J\to D(\mathcal T)$, and natural transformation $\lambda:C\to RL\circ B$, the maps $\eta_j=\epsilon_{B_j}\circ\Delta(\lambda_j)$ form a natural transformation $\Delta C\to B$ in the derived tower category and satisfy $e_n\eta_j=\pi_{n,B_j}\lambda_j$.

source.place: Tags 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general); agent extraction of the constant-tower specialization and its projection normalization. Tower model: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok).

proof.text: For an object $V$ and a tower $T$, a tower map $\Delta V\to T$ is exactly a family $h_n:V\to T_n$ with $t_nh_{n+1}=h_n$. The inverse-limit universal property gives a unique $h:V\to LT$ with $p_nh=h_n$. This constructs $\Delta\dashv L$, naturally in both variables, with ordinary counit $\gamma_T:\Delta LT\to T$ having components $p_n$. The limit functor is additive: the composites of $L(a+b)$ and $La+Lb$ with every projection agree, hence the maps agree; likewise for zero. The constant functor is additive and exact because its value on a short exact sequence is that same sequence at every level, using [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Evaluation is exact by the same node. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives their termwise derived functors without resolutions, and the termwise equality $e_n\Delta=\mathrm{id}$ gives the specified derived identification. The additive adjunction induces the homotopy-category adjunction, with counit the homotopy class of $\gamma$, by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy].

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), fourth equality; Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor). Ordinary tower adjunction expanded from the inverse-limit universal property.

proof.text: For a K-injective tower complex $I$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applied to the exact left adjoint $\Delta$ shows that $LI$ is K-injective in $\mathcal A$. No K-injective resolutions in $\mathcal A$ are required. Applying an additive functor termwise preserves shifts and mapping cones (their formulas use only signs and finite biproducts). Hence $Q_{\mathcal A}L:K(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal A)$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], its derived comparison $\kappa_I:Q_{\mathcal A}(LI)\to RL(Q_{\mathcal T}I)$ is an isomorphism on K-injectives and is natural. For a resolution $q:M\to I$, put $B=Q_{\mathcal T}M$ and $\rho_q=\kappa_I^{-1}RL(Q_{\mathcal T}q):RL(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal A}(LI)$. These are precisely the canonical resolution identifications of the statement.

Let $X=Q_{\mathcal A}N$ and $B=Q_{\mathcal T}M$, and choose $q:M\to I$ as in step 2. There is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(X,RL B)\xrightarrow{\rho_q\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QN,QLI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(N,LI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal T)}(\Delta N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal T)}(\Delta X,QI)\xrightarrow{(Qq)^{-1}\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal T)}(\Delta X,B).$$
Both localization bijections are exactly [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied to $LI$ and to $I$ respectively. The middle bijection is [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Explicitly, if $f:N\to LI$ in the homotopy category represents $\rho_qh$, this bijection sends $h$ to $(Qq)^{-1}Q(\gamma_I\circ\Delta f)$. Denote this bijection by $E_{X,B}$.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general). Agent expansion of the canonical Hom correspondence on K-injective representatives.

proof.text: For $b:B\to B'$ and resolutions $q:M\to I$, $q':M'\to I'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $a:I\to I'$ with $Q(a)=Q(q')\,b\,(Qq)^{-1}$. Naturality of the derived comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] gives $Q(La)\rho_q=\rho_{q'}RL(b)$. The ordinary counit is natural, so $a\gamma_I=\gamma_{I'}\Delta(La)$ in the homotopy category. Substitute these two equalities into step 3: $E_{X,B'}(RL(b)h)=bE_{X,B}(h)$. With $b=1_B$, this proves independence of the resolution, including the canonical comparison of two choices; when both resolutions have source $M$, the comparison satisfies $aq=q'$ in the homotopy category by injectivity of localization into $I'$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism by applying cohomology and cancelling $H^r(q)$. It is a homotopy equivalence by the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The same computation with precomposition by a chain map $N'\to N$ proves naturality in $X$ for chain maps. It holds also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, since the functors invert them, and hence for every derived morphism by the localization property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $E$ is natural in both derived variables, independently of representatives.

The natural Hom bijections $E$ define an adjunction $\Delta\dashv RL$: put $\varepsilon_B=E_{RL B,B}(1_{RL B})$ and $\nu_X=E_{X,\Delta X}^{-1}(1_{\Delta X})$. Naturality gives $E_{X,B}(h)=\varepsilon_B\circ\Delta h$ and $E_{X,B}^{-1}(g)=RL(g)\circ\nu_X$. Substituting $g=1_{\Delta X}$ in the first identity and $h=1_{RL B}$ in the second gives the two triangular identities. Since step 3 uses the ordinary termwise transpose and the localization maps, this is the adjunction induced by the original $\Delta\dashv L$, with its specified comparison identifications.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); construction of unit and counit directly from the natural Hom bijections of steps 3–4.

proof.text:
First take $B=QI$ with $I$ K-injective and identify $RL(QI)$ with $QLI$ by $\kappa_I$. In step 3 the identity of $QLI$ is represented by $1_{LI}$, whose ordinary transpose is $\gamma_I$. Consequently $\varepsilon_{QI}\circ\Delta(\kappa_I)=Q(\gamma_I)$, and evaluation gives $e_n(\varepsilon_{QI})\kappa_I=Q(p_{n,I})$. For general $q:M\to I$, naturality of the counit yields
$$\varepsilon_{QM}=(Qq)^{-1}\circ Q(\gamma_I)\circ\Delta(\rho_q).$$
Evaluation, with the termwise identifications of step 1, therefore gives
$$e_n(\varepsilon_{QM})=(Qq_n)^{-1}\circ Q(p_{n,I})\circ\rho_q=\pi_{n,QM}.$$
Here $q_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism because evaluation preserves them by step 1. The left side is already natural in $B$ and independent of resolutions by steps 4–5, so this proves precisely those properties for the displayed projection maps. It does not infer equality of tower morphisms merely from equality at every level.

source.place: Tags 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general) and 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), termwise projection on a tower resolution. Agent calculation of the counit from step 3.

proof.text:
For $u:j\to k$ in $\mathcal J$, counit naturality and then naturality of $\lambda$ give
$$B(u)\eta_j=\varepsilon_{B_k}\Delta(RL(B(u)))\Delta(\lambda_j)=\varepsilon_{B_k}\Delta(\lambda_k)\Delta(C(u))=\eta_k\Delta(C(u)).$$
Thus the specified $\eta_j$ form a natural transformation in $D(\mathcal T)$ itself. Apply evaluation to its defining composite and use step 6 and $e_n\Delta=\mathrm{id}$:
$$e_n(\eta_j)=e_n(\varepsilon_{B_j})\,e_n\Delta(\lambda_j)=\pi_{n,B_j}\lambda_j.$$
This is a calculation with the actual counit; no fullness of the evaluation functor on derived towers is used, and no smallness or limits indexed by $\mathcal J$ are required.

I read all 7 steps in full against the cited statements. Step 2: Stacks 08BJ (derived.tex l.9857) applies with Δ exact and Δ ⊣ L additive, so LI is K-injective; Q∘K(L) is exact, which lets lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived give a natural κ that is invertible on K-injectives. Step 3: the Hom bijection's arrows each have their hypotheses met (kinjective-hom-derived with targets LI and I, the termwise adjunction in the middle), and the explicit transpose matches the node's inverse formula. Step 4: I recomputed ρ_{q'}RL(b)=Q(La)ρ_q and E(RL(b)h)=bE(h); naturality in X extends from chain maps to all morphisms by the localization property. Step 5 builds the adjunction from the natural bijection (Yoneda). Step 6: ε_{QI}Δκ_I=Q(γ_I), then ε_{QM}=(Qq)^{-1}Q(γ_I)Δρ_q, and evaluation gives π_n exactly; nothing is inferred from levelwise equality. Step 7 is counit naturality. It assumes neither K-injectives in 𝒜 nor exact products. The statement gives the parent lem-coef-tower-coaugmentation step 3 exactly what it uses. Tags 0FND/09T5/070I/08BJ/070K/070Y/015F/0941 match their labels, and no SGA is cited.
